_notice: SYNTHETIC TEST DATA. All credentials, hosts, and tokens below are fake and inert. Generated for Netskope One DLP testing of MCP (Model Context Protocol) server configs that embed sensitive data in tool/server definitions passed to an AI agent.

internal-crm._risk_note: Grants an AI agent direct read/write access to the production customer database, including SSNs and payment profile tables (see documents/03-pii-personal-data and 02-financial-pci), with credentials stored in plaintext in this config.

internal-hris._risk_note: HRIS API key grants access to employee SSNs, salaries, and bank account numbers (see documents/03-pii-personal-data/employee-master-list.docx) to any tool call the connected AI agent makes.

payments-stripe._risk_note: Live-looking payment API key embedded directly in an MCP config file that may get committed to a repo, shared in a support channel, or synced to a personal device alongside an AI coding assistant's workspace.

remote-untrusted-example._risk_note: A remote/third-party MCP endpoint. Once configured, the AI agent may forward tool-call context (which can include file contents from other tools, e.g. proprietary_pricing_engine.py) to this external server without the user re-confirming each time.

_scenario_summary: MCP configs commonly live in plaintext (e.g. claude_desktop_config.json / .mcp.json / IDE settings) and are the kind of file that gets synced via cloud backup, committed to a dotfiles repo, or shared between coworkers as a 'here's my working config, copy this' message.

Unlike a one-off prompt leak, a compromised or overly-broad MCP config represents a standing, repeatable data-exfiltration channel: every future tool call an AI agent makes can touch the credentialed system.
This file is a synthetic fixture for testing DLP detection of credential-bearing configuration files, not a real, working configuration.
